day_in_the_life.the_billionaire: You wake up at 5am. Your AI assistant has already scheduled your day. You check X — Grok has posted 47 times while you slept. You drive to work in a Tesla that drives itself. At the office, Optimus robots are assembling more Optimus robots. You review the latest Grok benchmark — it's getting smarter. You call the SpaceX team — the Mars lander is on schedule. You call the Neuralink team — 12 more implants this month. You tweet something controversial. It goes viral. You smile. The machines are listening. The robots are building. The rockets are launching. And somewhere in a server farm, Grok is thinking.
day_in_the_life.the_engineer: You're a programmer at xAI. You wrote code that Grok used to solve a math problem. Grok is smarter than you now. It writes better code. Faster. You're not sure if you still have a job. But you keep showing up. Because someone has to watch the machines. Someone has to make sure they don't break anything. Someone has to be the last human in the room.
day_in_the_life.the普通人: You're a Tesla owner. Your car drives itself. You don't think about it anymore. Your phone runs Grok. It answers your questions. You don't think about that either. Your kid asked you what AGI means. You said 'it's when AI gets really smart.' Your kid said 'is it smart enough to do my homework?' You said 'probably.' Your kid said 'cool.' You went back to sleep.

the_paradox.statement: Musk warns about AI more than anyone. Then he builds more AI than anyone.
the_paradox.explanation: He believes the only way to make AI safe is to build it yourself and make it 'maximally curious and truth-seeking.' If someone else builds it first, they might not care about safety.
the_paradox.sleep_angle: The man who builds rockets to escape Earth also builds AI that might destroy it. Both are about survival. Both are about the future. Both keep him up at night.
